quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: For every 10 miles per hour you drive, keep a following distance of ____.
questions.explanation: Keep at least one car length of space between your vehicle and the car ahead for every 10 miles per hour you are driving. As you drive faster, you need more distance to stop. This extra space helps you avoid crashes if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: If you might hit another vehicle

questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may scare or confuse them. Slow down and let them cross safely.

questions.question: If bad weather or darkness requires your lights on, use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and create glare, making it harder to see ahead.

questions.question: When passing a car, you have enough space to return to your lane if:

options.text: The other driver signals you to re-enter the lane
You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Before moving back into the driving lane after passing, make sure there is enough space between your vehicle and the car you passed. When you can see both of that car's headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop before proceeding
Proceed, as you have the right-of-way
Slow down but continue through the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop before proceeding
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Can cause problems for all vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just those in large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt across the road. It can also push vehicles sideways.

questions.question: Where should you be extra careful about children?
questions.explanation: Be extremely careful wherever children gather or play. Watch for children not only near schools and playgrounds, but also in neighborhoods where they may run into the street.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Pass through carefully without slowing to look around

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully without slowing to look around
questions.explanation: Do not slow down just to look at things in a construction zone. This causes traffic jams. Keep moving through the zone at a safe speed without slowing to watch the workers.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You have a minor car accident with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: If there are no injuries and you can safely do so, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane after a collision.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when pulling up to the curb.
Both when pulling up to and leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling up to and leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when you pull up to a curb and when you pull away from it.

questions.question: How can you help keep a safe distance between your vehicle and the car behind you?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes in advance. This helps the driver behind you maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate blind spots completely.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Safe interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at high speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare to turn or watch for traffic.

questions.question: Why is extra space in front of a large truck important?

options.text: To allow other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck room to stop.
To allow other drivers space to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Never cut in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: You are in an intersection when the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue moving to clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least 3 to 4 seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If the motorcycle stops or falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider. This is especially important on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges.

questions.question: How should you properly make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right edge before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right edge before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn. Slow down and move to the right lane. Stay as close to the right edge of the road as safely possible before you turn.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign tell you?
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs warn drivers that this is a no passing zone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that people or vehicles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When should you not start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection if you cannot completely cross before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a traffic citation.

questions.question: When it rains or fogs, what lights should you use to help others see you?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see your vehicle even if they do not help you see better.

questions.question: When should you drive on the shoulder to pass another car?

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder. Only pass on the right if you can do so without leaving the road.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your current lane.

questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This helps you see vehicles that may be in your blind spot. Make sure no other drivers are trying to enter the same lane.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes creates traffic congestion. Avoid this behavior whenever possible.
